liebermann.description_de: Pseudo-Ingulf, angeblich Abt von Crowland († 1108), in Wahrheit ein Compilator um 1330
liebermann.shelfmark_as_given: Pseudo-Ingulf, Historia Croylandensis (a chronicle forged at Crowland c. 1330)
liebermann.notes: The Pseudo-Ingulf chronicle, a forgery compiled for Crowland c. 1330, which took over Leis Wl, with many misreadings, from an exemplar written before 1300 that was not the original of the Leis (1090–1135). Several copyists of I deliberately left out the Leis; for the others see il, Im, Io, Isp.

entries.text_de:
Pseudo-Ingulf, angeblich Abt von Crowland († 1108), in Wahrheit ein zu und für Crowland fälschender Compilator um 13302, der aus ‘alter’, also vor 1300 geschriebener, Vorlage Leis Wl, u. S. 492, mit vielen Lesefehlern aufnahm. Sie war mit dem Original der Leis (1090—1135) nicht identisch.

Mehrere Abschreiber I's liessen die Leis absichtlich fort3, über die anderen vgl. il, Im, Io, Isp.

il Vorlage für I und L[ateinischen Übersetzer der Leis Wl, u. S. 492].

Andere Hs. il, für Cn Vorlage von l und In Cn, stand aq nahe.
entries.text_en:
Pseudo-Ingulf, allegedly abbot of Crowland († 1108), in truth a compiler forging at and for Crowland c. 13302, who took in Leis Wl, below, p. 492, from an ‘old’ exemplar, i.e. one written before 1300, with many misreadings. That exemplar was not identical with the original of the Leis (1090—1135).

Several copyists of I deliberately left out the Leis3; on the others cf. il, Im, Io, Isp.

il exemplar for I and for L[the Latin translator of the Leis Wl, below, p. 492].

Another MS il, for Cn the exemplar of l and In Cn, stood close to aq.

notes.text_de: vgl. Neues Archiv ält. Dt. Gesch. 18, 262; Archiv neu. Spra. CVI 114.
notes.text_en: cf. Neues Archiv ält. Dt. Gesch. 18, 262; Archiv neu. Spra. CVI 114.

notes.text_de: Darunter Arundel 178, 16. Jh., von Birch The chron. of Croyland edirt.
notes.text_en: Among them Arundel 178, 16th century, edited by Birch, The chron. of Croyland.

transcription.doubts: The two paragraphs on il (printed with il in bold at the start of a paragraph, not as a centred heading) are taken as part of the I entry. 'In Cn' in the last paragraph appears to be roman, not bold (contrast bold Cn just before). The dagger before 1108 is printed as †.
